subject.title: [Bug] WebChat: optimistic USER messages are lost (not just hidden) when chat.send returns before the durable transcript lands — full-replace history reconcile drops them

question: Should WebChat `chat.send` keep returning `started` before the user turn is durably visible in `chat.history`, or should the Gateway require a durable user-turn write or visible failure/retry contract before that ACK?
rationale: Current main fixes the client-side full-replace symptom, but the remaining server-side behavior affects transcript ordering, duplicate suppression, before-message hooks, session rollover, and existing in-flight workflows; that is a product/compatibility decision rather than a safe autonomous cleanup.

options.title: Narrow the Gateway persistence PR
options.body: Review or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80670 with a smaller durable user-turn persistence path that proves no duplicate transcript rows and no redaction bypass.

options.title: Accept current UI-side mitigation
options.body: Close the issue only if maintainers decide that preserving the visible optimistic bubble and idempotency correlation is sufficient even though ACK still precedes durable persistence.

options.title: Define a visible failure contract
options.body: Keep ACK fast but require a visible WebChat error/retry path when dispatch or persistence does not actually begin.

recommendation.title: Narrow the Gateway persistence PR
recommendation.body: Review or replace https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/80670 with a smaller durable user-turn persistence path that proves no duplicate transcript rows and no redaction bypass.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merger/contributor on WebChat pending-send behavior and user-turn transcript persistence, with the best available routing signal for the product contract choice.
